lesson.title: More Decisions
lesson.driving_question: How can a program sort a value into one of several outcomes?
lesson.primary_concept_family: An if/elif/else chain checks ordered comparison conditions.
misconceptions: elif is checked only after earlier if conditions are false.
The first true branch runs and the remaining branches are skipped.
Comparison operators include the boundary when they use >= or <=.
else does not have a condition.

code_expectations: Use one indented print() per branch.
Keep the final else as the catch-all outcome.

primm.prompt: Recall how an if/else statement chooses one of two paths. What type of value does int(input()) produce?
Use the exact input 7. Write the result of each comparison and predict the one message that will appear. Explain why the final else is not reached.
Run the supplied file with 7. Compare the result with your prediction, then test one score from each range.

questions: If you enter 8, which message appears? Which comparison is True?
If score >= 5 is checked first, what message would a score of 9 receive?
If you enter 5, which message appears?
Why does a value that matches no earlier condition run the else block without another comparison?

primm.prompt: A score of 9 should now count as Excellent. Adjust the first comparison, then prove the boundary by running scores 8 and 9 and recording the two different results.
Add one elif branch so scores 3 and 4 display "Keep practising". Scores below 3 should display "Try again"; the Excellent and Good outcomes stay unchanged.
Create a temperature classifier with three outcomes: Hot at 30 or above, Warm from 20 to 29, and Cool below 20. Test 19, 20 and 30.
Repair the comparison boundary and the output variable. Test one score in every outcome.

blocks.definition: A comparison checks two values and produces True or False. Comparisons help a program choose an outcome.
elif means else if. It checks another condition when the earlier if condition was False.
>= means greater than or equal to. The boundary value is included.
Python checks an if/elif/else chain from top to bottom. The first True branch runs, then the chain ends.
A classifier puts an input into one named group. if, elif and else make the groups exclusive.
